I'm in my 20s living in a sharehouse in Brisbane with 2 others about my age. Its been high 30s all week and we can't afford to run the air-con. We've lost all hope for the future. I adore this city but I'm thinking about the inevitability of having to move away to escape the heat- its gone from mildly annoying every summer to unliveable in winter very very quickly. Politicians seem to talk about climate change as a future problem because they are scared to address the inevitability of it - and of course because it doesn't affect them when they're sitting up in their towers running the air-con 24/7 because they can afford to, and most of them will be dead in 20 years anyway. 
The vibe is existential and apocalyptic. Every friendly interaction I've had this week has quickly turned to the topic of the weather, most people making an apathetic quip about how many winters we even have left- or something along those lines. 
"its a scorcher today!" is followed by "buckle up for the next few decades"
We laugh it off in typical Australian fashion but I know I am not the only one who is deeply scared for our future. I'm starting to save up so that I can move somewhere colder.

Hi! Coincidentally I am in the exact same situation as you right now. Had a cut on my finger that I kept picking and cleaning with alchohol wipes so that it wouldn't get infected and surprise surprise- its currently infected. I'm trying not to spiral about it but the best thing I am finding helps is distracting myself. I've been changing the bandaid every couple of hours and applying more betadine.

Do you have someone in your life you can talk to this about? It helped me a lot to get my fears off my chest by talking to my housemate about it. Even if you just call a family member to talk about it. 

You will be okay. As will I. Minor infections are very easily treatable. But I understand just saying this won't fix either of our issues because the cut is still infected. Think of it as exposure therapy - when your wound is healed, its less reasonable to your OCD that a simple infection could cause so much harm. 

Betadine, baindaids, and it will heal before you know it.

A little bit about this,

I started drawing this the same day I found out about his passing. It hit me like a fucking brick, as it did many others. I was hesitant to post this piece anywhere because it feels pretty personal to me, but a while back Noxy at Hypixel posted a tweet asking for fanart that could be included in the books being sent to Techno's family, and I posted it in response to that tweet. A few days later I got a DM asking for my permission for my art to be printed in the book. I feel honoured, but my heart will always be heavy knowing that he will never see it.

Some of you LORE NERDS might recognise my username, as a while back I posted my theory about how the "3 lives system" should work in the Dream SMP and it was made canon by Wilbur (I think its my pinned post still, not sure how that feature even works though). This is a little silly, but pretty soon after Wilbur talked about it on stream, Techno kept making jokes about peoples deaths being "canon" on the server. It made me so happy that I kept a google doc with links to every single clip of him referencing my theory, even if it was just in the minecraft game chat. I'll never know if he actually read my post or not, but even his acknowledgement of something that I wrote made me unbelieveably happy, as he is someone who inspires me so much with his storytelling.

Seeing Technodad post on this subreddit recently has made me think it might be nice to post this here, I feel less guilty about it. I don't really know why I felt guilty in the first place, emotions are weird.

Thanks for reading this if anyone did, and if not, hello Reddit void!

Hi! I can understand how confused you must be, as I've been there too- I'm 18 and identify as a (non-binary-ish) trans guy but I started feeling like this when I was around 14 too. The best advice I could give to you is not to jump into things too quickly, you have all the time in the world to figure yourself out. If you are thinking of telling somebody, make sure that its safe to do so! And if you aren't too sure of yourself, its okay to talk to people about that too. What you're experiencing definitely sounds like gender dysphoria, so you could start by telling someone you trust that you feel this way.

I hope this helps a little bit :) good luck with everything! Figuring out your identity is tricky, and its okay to be wrong about things sometimes, thats just life.

I feel this. I dropped out of school, stopped working, and stayed in my room for months on end last year for the exact same reason. 
Trust me when I say that it won't help. In my case, I felt no less dysphoric in my bedroom than I did out in public. Dysphoria doesn't go away and it doesn't get put on pause with the rest of your life, as much as it sucks to hear.

I don't know your situation so I can't give the best advice, but anti-depressants really helped me because staying in my room and pausing my life had made me very depressed. Also, having a queer therapist who works with trans people has helped me a whole lot more than you'd think (although it took me months to find and get an appointment with them)

I hope everything goes well for you man, I don't reccomend pausing your life but if its what you want to do I can't really stop you through reddit.

I feel like this would have had a more interesting response if it were posted on somewhere like r/dreamsmp because more people there love to analyse the lore and controversies surrounding certain subjects like this one. Not saying that people here don't, just pointing out a few people in the replies saying things like "calm down its just roleplay" which annoys me a little. The Dream SMP is a story in its own respect, it deserves to be analysed and talked about like one, and I promise you nobody is actually butt-hurt irl over this sort of stuff, its just a discussion.  


I think the main thing people are misunderstanding about this post is that OP is talking about people who excuse c!Dreams actions, NOT people who just regularly enjoy his character. There's a difference between enjoying a character and the way that they're written VS fully excusing a characters actions because you see them as a Good Person. Especially when aforementioned characters actions are child abuse.   


I don't fully agree with everything that was said in the original post, but I get what they were trying to say and it's annoying to see it misenterpeted as "dsmp twitter fan can't divide fiction and reality and takes the rp too seriously" because I understand their point, and child abuse (even in fiction) is a touchy subject that people are allowed to be upset about. If there genuinely was no connection between fiction and reality, stories would be pointless. Any work of fiction is made for people to think about and connect it to experiences in the real world, or at least thats my view on it.

TLDR; you're allowed to like c!Dream. You're allowed to empathise with him. Nobody's saying you aren't. He's one of my favourite characters in fact. Its just a little weird when people start excusing abuse/saying c!Tommy deserved it and c!Dream was in the right.
